legend: The scientists invented the new UL-2018 processor that is able to quickly process arrays in some special way. A key feature of its architecture is the separation operation of a segment of the array.

Consider an array [a1,a2,…,an]%%ZSMJ0%%. The separation operation is characterized by two integers L%%ZSMJ1%% and R%%ZSMJ2%%. Let S(L,R)%%ZSMJ3%% denote the operation of the segment [aL,aL+1,…,aR]%%ZSMJ4%%. Executing the S(L,R)%%ZSMJ5%% operation reorders the elements in this segment as follows. First, the elements aL+1,aL+3,aL+5,…%%ZSMJ6%% are taken, that is elements ai%%ZSMJ7%% that i−L%%ZSMJ8%% is odd. Their relative order remains unchanged. Then, the elements aL,aL+2,aL+4,…%%ZSMJ9%% are taken (ai%%ZSMJ10%% that i−L%%ZSMJ11%% is even). These retain the relative order too.

For example, consider the array [2,4,1,5,3,6,7,8]%%ZSMJ12%%. Applying the operation S(2,6)%%ZSMJ13%% changes the segment [4,1,5,3,6]%%ZSMJ14%% into [1,3,4,5,6]%%ZSMJ15%%, so the entire array becomes [2,1,3,4,5,6,7,8]%%ZSMJ16%%.

To demonstrate the capabilities of the new processor, the scientists decided to use separation operations to sort an array of distinct numbers. You will be given an array of size n%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤n≤3000%%ZSMJ18%%) with distinct numbers from 1%%ZSMJ19%% to n%%ZSMJ20%%. You must sort it in ascending order using no more than 15000%%ZSMJ21%% separation operations.

For example, the mentioned array [2,4,1,5,3,6,7,8]%%ZSMJ22%% can be sorted in two separation operations. First, apply S(2,6)%%ZSMJ23%% to get [2,1,3,4,5,6,7,8]%%ZSMJ24%%, and then the operation S(1,2)%%ZSMJ25%% makes the array sorted increasingly: [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]%%ZSMJ26%%.

Your task is to write a program that for a given array determines the sequence of at most 15000%%ZSMJ27%% separation operations, after which the specified array will be sorted in ascending order. It isn't necessary to minimize the number of operations performed (just use at most 15000%%ZSMJ28%%).
input: The first line of the input contains an integer n%%ZSMJ29%% — the number of elements in the given array (1≤n≤3000%%ZSMJ30%%).
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ31%% distinct integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ32%% — the elements of the given array (1≤ai≤n%%ZSMJ33%%, all ai%%ZSMJ34%% are different).
output: The first line of the output should contain an integer k%%ZSMJ35%% — the number of separation operations performed (0≤k≤15000%%ZSMJ36%%).

In the following k%%ZSMJ37%% lines, you should print the description of the operations, in the order they are executed. Each operation is described by two integers L%%ZSMJ38%% and R%%ZSMJ39%% — the beginning and the end of the segment to which the separation operation should be applied (1≤L≤R≤n%%ZSMJ40%%).

Note that you don't have to minimize the number k%%ZSMJ41%%. You can output any sequence of separation operations that contains at most 15000%%ZSMJ42%% operations and sorts the given array in ascending order. It is guaranteed that at least one such sequence exists.
You will get points for a group if you pass all tests in this group and all groups listed in the dependencies. The group 0%%ZSMJ44%% denotes the sample test(s) from the statement.
note: The second sample test is analyzed in detail in the problem statement.
In the third sample test, there is a solution with a single separation operation, but since you don't have to minimize the number of operations, the provided output is also correct.
